explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a Python-based data-pipeline/automation tool rather than a classic client-server “full-stack” app. It’s an experiment framework where a decision engine (ChatGPT) consumes market data each trading day, applies rules, emits trade instructions, logs them to CSV, and generates performance visualizations.  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   Top-level directories and files:  
   • Experiment Details – research artifacts, prompts, Q&A, disclaimers.  
   • Scripts and CSV Files – core scripts (Generate_Graph.py, Trading_Script.py) plus generated CSV logs (chatgpt_portfolio_update.csv, chatgpt_trade_log.csv).  
   • Start Your Own – a “template” copy of the core scripts and CSV files for bootstrapping a new experiment.  
   • Weekly Deep Research (MD/PDF) – weekly summary documents in Markdown and PDF.  
   • trading_script.py (root) – duplicate/entry-point for live trading logic.  
   • requirements.txt – Python dependencies (pandas, yfinance, matplotlib, OpenAI/ChatGPT SDK).  

   Architectural choices:  
   • Modular scripts separate data ingestion + decision logic (trading_script.py) from visualization (Generate_Graph.py).  
   • CSV files as simple persistent storage.  
   • “Start Your Own” directory as a scaffold for new experiments.  

3. Examine README for additional insights  
   - Tech stack: Python, pandas + yfinance (market data), Matplotlib (visuals), ChatGPT (trade decisions).  
   - Workflow: daily data feed → ChatGPT decision engine → strict stop-loss + trade generator → CSV log updates → weekly performance graphs.  

4. How to draw the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
      1. Data Ingestion Module  
         • yFinance API call (pandas)  
         • Input: list of micro-cap tickers, historical price data  
      2. Decision Engine  
         • Core Python logic + orchestration  
         • External dependency: ChatGPT API (LLM prompts/responses)  
         • Business rules: stop-loss, portfolio rebalancing  
      3. Execution & Persistence  
         • Writes trade orders and portfolio updates to CSV logs (chatgpt_trade_log.csv, chatgpt_portfolio_update.csv)  
         • (Optionally) Broker API if real trades are executed  
      4. Visualization Module  
         • Generate_Graph.py  
         • Reads CSV logs, produces Matplotlib charts comparing performance vs Russell 2K  
      5. Documentation & Research Store  
         • Experiment Details, Weekly Deep Research MD/PDF  
         • Static assets for research, prompts, disclaimers  

   b. Relationships & interactions  
      1. Daily scheduler/cron kicks off Data Ingestion → Decision Engine  
      2. Decision Engine ↔ ChatGPT API (prompt/response round-trip)  
      3. Decision Engine → Execution & Persistence (CSV writes)  
      4. Visualization Module → reads CSV logs → outputs PNG or console graphs  
      5. “Start Your Own” directory – a template that wires the same flow end-to-end  

   c. Architectural patterns & design principles  
      • Pipeline pattern: data flows sequentially through modules  
      • Separation of concerns: ingestion, decision-making, persistence, visualization each in separate scripts  
      • Template directory for easy project bootstrap (Start Your Own)  
      • Use of flat files (CSV) for simplicity and transparency  

   d. Key technologies/frameworks  
      • Python 3.x  
      • pandas + yfinance (market data ingestion)  
      • OpenAI ChatGPT SDK (LLM interface)  
      • Matplotlib (visualization)  
      • CSV as data store (trade logs, portfolio updates)  
      • Markdown/PDF for research docs  

5. Tailoring the diagram to this project type  
   - Emphasize the daily data-decision-execution loop.  
   - Show the “template” (Start Your Own) as a parallel path or sub-diagram.  
   - Highlight CSV logs as both output of execution and input to visualization.  
   - Represent research docs as annotations or side-storage, not in the critical path.  

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Use clear rectangular boxes for modules (Data Ingestion, Decision Engine, Execution, Visualization, Research Store).  
   - Draw arrows to indicate data flow and dependencies (e.g., yFinance → Decision Engine; Decision Engine → ChatGPT API; Decision Engine → CSV; CSV → Visualization).  
   - Color-code:  
     • Blue for data flow components (Ingestion, CSV storage)  
     • Green for compute logic (Decision Engine, ChatGPT API)  
     • Orange for output/visualization (graphs)  
     • Gray for documentation artifacts (research folder)  
   - Label each arrow with the data format or protocol (e.g., JSON over HTTPS for ChatGPT API, CSV read/write for logs).  
   - Use a legend explaining shapes and colors.  

7. Level of detail  
   - Be explicit about file/script names in each component box (e.g., trading_script.py under Decision Engine).  
   - Show “Start Your Own” as a duplication of core scripts, or as a sub-flow box.  
   - Optionally annotate the frequency of execution (daily, weekly).  
   - Don’t omit the research directories entirely—they provide context but sit off to the side.  

By following these steps, you’ll produce a detailed architecture diagram that clearly separates ingestion, decision-making, execution, visualization, and documentation, while calling out the key technologies and data flows that define the ChatGPT Micro-Cap Experiment.  
</explanation>
